issues.legal_issue: An appellate court must consider a pending application to adduce additional evidence before deciding the appeal, and may admit evidence only when a prescribed ground for doing so is established.
material_facts: In a second appeal, the appellant sought to place official records before the High Court as additional evidence.

The High Court had directed the Collector to produce an acquisition notification, and the Collector reported that no such notification existed because the land belonged to the government; the report also referred to compensation paid to the former holder.

The High Court dismissed the second appeal without considering the pending additional-evidence application or referring to the Collector’s report, although the records appeared capable of affecting the dispute about whether the decree had been obtained by concealment or fraud.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred by failing to consider the application before deciding the appeal. Its orders were set aside and the matter remitted for the application to be decided on its merits; the Supreme Court expressed no final view on whether the evidence should be admitted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 107 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Order 41 Rule 27 create an exception to the general rule against introducing new evidence on appeal. Under Order 41 Rule 27(1), additional evidence may be admitted if the lower court wrongly refused evidence that ought to have been admitted; if, despite due diligence, the evidence was not known or could not have been produced earlier; or if the appellate court requires it to pronounce judgment or for another substantial cause. Under clause (b), the court must itself find the evidence needful; it may be needed to enable judgment or to clarify an obscurity so that judgment can be given more satisfactorily. The court must consider the application before deciding the appeal. These principles are drawn from Parsotim Thakur v. Lal Mohar Thakur and K. Venkataramiah v. A. Seetharama Reddy.

predicates.second_appeal_pending: A party’s appeal is pending before an appellate court as a second appeal.
predicates.additional_evidence_application_filed: A party has asked the appellate court to admit or obtain evidence not included in the record below.

issues.definition: When a second appeal is pending and a party has applied to introduce additional evidence, the appellate court must consider that application before deciding the appeal on its merits.

issues.legal_issue: A request to amend pleadings cannot be rejected as unmaintainable merely because it is made during a second appeal and must instead be assessed under the governing amendment principles.
material_facts: During the second appeal, the appellant applied to amend its written statement and later sought permission to urge additional grounds supporting that application.
The High Court rejected the amendment application solely on the ground that such an application could not be entertained at the second-appeal stage.
The Supreme Court concluded that the application had not been considered from the correct perspective and remitted it for a decision on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in rejecting the amendment application solely because it was made during a second appeal. The application had to be considered on its merits under the applicable principles, without the Supreme Court deciding whether the amendment should ultimately be allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, as it stood at the relevant time, permits amendment of pleadings at any stage of the proceedings. Under Pirgonda Hongonda Patil v. Kalgonda Shidgonda Patil, an amendment should be allowed when it is necessary to determine the real questions in controversy and does not work injustice to the other side. It should be refused where the other party cannot be restored to the position it would have occupied had the pleading originally been correct and the resulting injury cannot be compensated in costs. Gajanan Jaikishan Joshi v. Prabhakar Mohanlal Kalwar is also cited.

predicates.second_appeal_pending: A party’s appeal is pending before an appellate court as a second appeal.
predicates.amendment_application_filed: A party has asked the court to amend a pleading during the proceedings.

issues.definition: When a pleading-amendment request is made during a pending second appeal, the court must decide it on its merits rather than reject it solely because of the stage of the proceedings.
